channel.title: VivaVoltia – Home Solar Guides
channel.description: Independent guides to residential solar energy for US homeowners.

item.title: The Complete Guide to Home Solar in 2026
item.description: Our complete home solar guide for 2026: what a system costs without the federal credit, how to size it, pick equipment and batteries, and find incentives.

item.title: Solar Incentives by State in 2026: What's Left After the Federal Credit
item.description: Solar incentives by state in 2026: state tax credits, rebates, SRECs, and tax exemptions that still cut costs now that the federal homeowner credit is gone.

item.title: How to Compare Solar Quotes: A 10-Point Checklist
item.description: How to compare solar quotes on price per watt, equipment, production estimates, warranties, and financing, plus the sales red flags to watch for in 2026.

item.title: How Much Does a Solar Battery Cost in 2026?
item.description: Solar battery cost in 2026: about $10,000–$16,000 installed for 10–15 kWh. Prices by size and brand, what drives cost, and when a battery pays for itself.

item.title: Solar With or Without a Battery: Which Makes More Sense?
item.description: Solar with or without a battery? How your utility's export credits, rate plan, outage risk, and budget decide whether home storage is worth the extra cost.

item.title: California NEM 3.0 Explained: Is Solar Still Worth It Under Net Billing?
item.description: California NEM 3.0 explained: how the Net Billing Tariff cut export credits about 75%, why it was upheld in 2026, and how to design solar that still pays off.

item.title: Do Solar Panels Work on Cloudy Days, in Rain, and in Snow?
item.description: Do solar panels work on cloudy days? Yes, at reduced output. What to expect from solar in clouds, rain, snow, cold, and heat, and how installers plan for it.

item.title: The Solar Installation Process: Step-by-Step Timeline
item.description: The solar installation process step by step: quote to permission to operate takes about 1–3 months; rooftop work just 1–3 days. Tips to avoid delays.

item.title: Solar Panel Orientation and Tilt: Which Roof Direction Is Best?
item.description: The best direction for solar panels in the US is south, but east and west roofs lose only 10–20%. How orientation and tilt affect output on your roof.

item.title: Hybrid vs. Grid-Tie Inverters: Which Do You Need?
item.description: Hybrid vs. grid-tie inverter: how they differ, AC vs. DC coupling, costs, and which to choose if you want a solar battery now or might add one later.

item.title: How Many Solar Batteries Do You Need to Go Off-Grid?
item.description: How many batteries do you need to go off-grid? Size storage from daily kWh, days of autonomy, and winter sun, with worked examples and realistic costs.

item.title: How Shade Affects Solar Panels (and How Optimizers Help)
item.description: How solar panel shading cuts output, how bypass diodes, optimizers, and microinverters reduce the losses, and when trimming trees is the better fix.

item.title: Portable Power Station vs. Home Battery for Emergency Backup
item.description: Portable power station vs. home battery for outages: compare capacity, power, cost, and safety to decide which backup option fits your home and budget.

item.title: Can Hail Damage Solar Panels? Ratings, Risks, and Insurance
item.description: Can hail damage solar panels? Panels are tested to survive 1-inch hail at about 51 mph. What hail ratings mean, insurance coverage, and steps after a storm.

item.title: Charging an EV With Solar Panels: How Many Panels Do You Need?
item.description: Charging an EV with solar panels: a typical EV adds 3,000–4,500 kWh a year, or about 6–9 extra panels. Sizing, costs, charging tips, and 2026 incentives.

item.title: Do Solar Panels Work During a Power Outage?
item.description: Do solar panels work during a power outage? Most grid-tied systems shut off for safety. Why, and three ways to keep your power on with solar and batteries.

item.title: What Is Net Metering? How Solar Bill Credits Work in 2026
item.description: What is net metering? How solar bill credits work, net metering vs. net billing, true-up periods, and how your state's policy changes the value of solar.

item.title: What Are Monocrystalline Solar Panels? Types, Efficiency, and Cost
item.description: Monocrystalline solar panels explained: how they work, how they compare with polycrystalline and thin-film, and what TOPCon and back-contact cells mean.

item.title: The 30% Federal Solar Tax Credit Ended: What Homeowners Need to Know in 2026
item.description: The 30% federal solar tax credit ended December 31, 2025. Who can still claim it, how leases still benefit, and which solar incentives remain in 2026.

item.title: Tesla Solar Roof vs. Traditional Solar Panels: Cost and Performance Compared
item.description: Tesla Solar Roof vs. solar panels: solar roofs cost two to three times more per watt. Compare cost, efficiency, durability, and when each one makes sense.

item.title: Tesla Powerwall 3 Review (2026): Specs, Price, and Who It's For
item.description: Tesla Powerwall 3 review for 2026: 13.5 kWh, 11.5 kW output, built-in solar inverter, and $13,000–$16,500 installed. Real backup runtimes and alternatives.

item.title: Solar Lease vs. Buy in 2026: Which Is the Better Deal?
item.description: Solar lease vs. buy in 2026: how cash, loans, leases, and PPAs compare now that only leasing companies get a federal credit, and the contract terms to check.

item.title: Microinverters vs. String Inverters: Which Is Best for Your Home?
item.description: Microinverters vs. string inverters: how each works, costs, shade performance, lifespan, and rapid shutdown rules, plus where power optimizers fit in.

item.title: How Much Do Solar Panels Cost for a 2,000 Sq Ft House in 2026?
item.description: How much do solar panels cost for a 2,000 sq ft house? Typically $19,000–$25,000 for 7–9 kW in 2026, plus battery prices and realistic payback times.

item.title: How Many Solar Panels Do I Need? A Step-by-Step Sizing Guide
item.description: How many solar panels do I need? Size your system in four steps using your electric bill, local sun hours, and panel wattage, with tables for typical homes.

item.title: How Long Do Solar Panels Last? Lifespan, Degradation, and Warranties
item.description: How long do solar panels last? Usually 25–30+ years, losing about 0.5% of output per year per NREL. What wears out first and how panel warranties work.

item.title: Do Solar Panels Need Maintenance? Cleaning, Monitoring, and Costs
item.description: Solar panel maintenance is minimal: what routine care involves, when and how to clean panels safely, how to spot problems with monitoring, and typical costs.

item.title: Do Solar Panels Increase Home Value? What the Research Says
item.description: Do solar panels increase home value? Zillow and Berkeley Lab research found buyers pay more for owned solar. How much, why leases differ, and how to prove it.

item.title: Can an HOA Stop You From Installing Solar Panels?
item.description: Can an HOA stop you from installing solar panels? How state solar access laws limit HOA rules, examples from CA, TX, and FL, and how to get approved fast.

item.title: Can You Install Solar Panels on a Metal Roof? Pros, Cons, and Mounting Options
item.description: Installing solar panels on a metal roof: how standing seam clamps avoid drilling, how corrugated roofs are handled, costs, and what to check before you start.
